newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SE Asian Grain - Corn prices steady to easier.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Grain - Corn prices steady to easier.

text.p: Southeast Asian corn prices were steady to easier this week with high stocks, ample imports and pressure from domestic harvest supplies keeping a lid on the market, regional traders said on Wednesday.

In Malaysia, both corn and wheat prices were quoted lower as feedmillers, farm owners and flour companies were comfortable with adequate stocks in their silos and waiting to pick up bargains, local traders said.
Bulk corn was priced at between 520-530 ringgit ($208-$212) a tonne ex-factory/godown in the central region, down from last week's 530-540 ringgit level.

"A" grade wheat in bags was steady at 880 ringgit ($353) a tonne ex-factory/godown central region. But low-grade wheat was offered in a much lower range of 550-600 ringgit ($220-$240) from the previous week's 580-600 ($233-$241) level.
"The market's been pretty quiet the whole of last week," said a Kuala Lumpur flour mill official. "There's enough corn in the silos of big farms and enough wheat in the flour mills."
Traders said one corn dealing house was depressing local corn prices further by selling about 10 ringgit below the average market price.
They said the company had even sold bulk corn at between 500-510 ringgit three weeks ago when the average price was between 550-560 ringgit.
The Kuala Lumpur-based dealing house declined comment when contacted by Reuters.
"The company is getting its stock cheaply from a flour mill which overbought about 150,000 tonnes of corn earlier in the year," said a trader.

"Even some big feedmills are buying from this company now and this is affecting local corn prices to an extent," said the trader, adding that smaller farms and end-users still relied on spot purchases in the local market.
Soymeal stabilised at 760 ringgit ($305) a tonne after speculation last week that Malaysian dealers had bought large quantities of Indian soymeal was not confirmed.
In Thailand, domestic maize/corn prices paid by feed producers were steady this week, despite increased supply from the new domestic harvest, as buyers slowed their purchases.
The price of 14.50 percent-moisture maize was quoted at an average of between 4.16-4.25 baht a kg, barely changed from last week when it averaged 4.20 baht.
The supply was also affected by rain which hampered transportation, traders said.
The deadline to import maize under the government's low- tariff programme ended on June 30. Only 299,756 tonnes of maize out of a 550,000-tonne quota was covered.
Locally crushed high-protein domestic soymeal firmed further to 10.25 baht a kg from 9.90 baht a week ago as Thai feed millers awaited delivery of imports from Brazil.
Soymeal crushed locally from imported beans was quoted at 9.70-9.75 baht a kg from 9.50 baht a week ago, traders said.

They said feedmillers had ordered 50,000 tonnes of low quality soymeal from Brazil for August-September shipment. It was expected to arrive in Thailand by October. The price of the shipment was said to be below $300 a tonne C&F Bangkok.
Traders saw Thai soymeal prices rising further as local stocks are diminishing.

Oil crushers have slowed down crushing during the past few months as increased production of palm oil has affected demand for soy oil. "There is almost no soymeal left in warehouses," said one trader.
This year's small Thai wet season soybean crop being harvested from late August to early October and earlier limited soybean imports had also reduced soymeal stocks, he said.
In Indonesia, corn prices were also indicated steady at around 500 rupiah a kg for imports, but there were reports of sales being done as low as 490 rupiah, traders said.
"The price is steady as at the moment, buyers are not too aggressive and sellers, particularly in Lampung, are also not too aggressive," one trader said.

A shipment of 35,000 tonnes of corn, thought to be from Argentina, arrived in Indonesia this month as expected. About 70 percent of it was expected to be distributed quickly and sold at around the 500 rupiah mark.
Stocks in Lampung, Indonesia's main corn growing area, were said to be low, but local corn prices were steady at about 460 rupiah a kg, traders said.
They said soymeal prices had softened in the past week as the 60,000 tonnes of South American meal imported in August had weighed on the market.
Argentine 44 percent protein soymeal was quoted at 790 rupiah a kg and Indian 48 percent protein at 805 rupiah compared with 820 rupiah for both origins last week.
